label: accepted

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette all read as a stone archway (round-headed opening, piers, coping); front outline symmetric, A15 error 0.0 on X.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: big wall mass, medium pier quoins / voussoir ring / coping, small gold keystone.
evidence.V3: Top-heavy and stiff: a large blank spandrel slab sits over a narrow opening, and the voussoir ring and keystone are small for the wall, so the stylisation reads timid rather than chunky.
evidence.V4: Quoins, voussoirs and coping have consistent chamfers, but the main wall slab corners look razor-sharp in the end-section close-up.
evidence.V5: Flat keystone close-up shows a jagged notch on the keystone's right edge and irregular overlapping voussoir outlines (178 cross-shell overlaps); studio view otherwise clean.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in 3 values (dark base course, mid wall, light quoins/coping) plus one gold keystone accent; sandstone and basalt colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone hue with gold keystone exactly as the modular kit spec describes.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default (walkable arch), CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling along X passes with IoU 1.0.

evidence.V1: Arch doorway reads clearly from front, three-quarter and silhouette; symmetry_error X 0.0 and front outline is symmetric.
evidence.V2: Coursed pier blocks, voussoir ring and gold keystone give medium/small detail, but the whole upper wall above the arch is one large blank slab, so hierarchy is only partial.
evidence.V3: Blocky and stiff: narrow tall opening, coursing stops abruptly at the springing, plain lintel slab occupies the top half; pier blocks step out past the wall face (notches in silhouette).
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on pier blocks, voussoirs, keystone and top coping catch light in the springing and end-section close-ups.
evidence.V5: Close-ups clean; voussoir-to-pier junction at the springing is a designed step, no pinches or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone in three values (dark base course, mid, light) plus a gold keystone accent; colourways stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: LF_VertexColor single material, chamfered stone, gold keystone accent: kit-consistent.
evidence.V9: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default (walkable opening), CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 pass.

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette all read as a round-headed stone arch with a capped wall; front outline is symmetric (A15 X error 0.0) and the keystone is centred.
evidence.V2: Big (wall + opening) and small (voussoirs, gold keystone, coursed jamb blocks, coping) exist, but the upper spandrel is a large blank slab occupying ~40 % of the front, and the voussoir ring is thin relative to it, so the medium tier is weak.
evidence.V3: Coursed jambs with a lighter impost block and a coping lip give some style, but the tall narrow opening under a flat blank wall reads stiff; the voussoir ring is not chunky or exaggerated.
evidence.V4: Close_springing and close_end_section studio show even chamfers on every jamb block, voussoir and the coping, catching consistent highlight lines.
evidence.V5: Close-ups clean: no pinches, seams or z-fighting at the springing or keystone; the small jog on the keystone's right edge in the flat close-up is the chamfer meeting the adjacent voussoir, not a defect; A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (light impost/coping, mid wall, dark base course) plus one gold keystone accent; brick and sandstone colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone hue, gold keystone per wave-2 modular spec, kit-range chamfers; matches kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Default collision (walkable), CanTouch off, MeshPart white + SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes (iou 1.0).

artifacts: notch/tooth on the keystone's side edge and messy voussoir-wall intersections in flat light
top_fixes: Clean the keystone and voussoir intersections with the wall so their outlines are crisp in flat light
Enlarge the voussoir ring and keystone (and/or widen the opening) and break up the blank spandrel with block lines so the arch reads chunky and confident
Chamfer the main wall slab edges to match the quoins and kit
Break up the blank upper wall: continue stone coursing or add block outlines/ashlar joints above the arch
Widen the opening slightly and relate coursing heights to the voussoir ring so the springing transition feels designed
Give the keystone a little more projection/scale so the focal point reads at 64 px
Thicken the voussoir ring and let it stand proud of the wall so the arch is the dominant medium shape
Break up the blank upper spandrel (a string course, a few offset ashlar blocks or a slightly recessed panel)
Make the keystone chunkier and let it project above the voussoir line for a stronger stylised read
